propositions: When an LLM call raises an exception, control exits PydanticAIRunner.run() before reaching usage_log.record(), leaving no row written despite potential token spend
A run's spend total folded from the usage log JSONL under-reports actual spend by omitting failed calls, causing billable CI jobs to publish incomplete summaries
Per-step attribution cannot account for failed calls, making it impossible to identify which passes are expensive when a retry exhausts

Failed LLM calls must write usage rows with identifying fields (op, step, model_class, model, provider) and available token counters, distinguishable from successful calls by an explicit outcome marker
Telemetry logging must never convert a provider exception into a different error nor swallow the original exception, preserving the call path through the failure
Retried calls must not double-count: a failed attempt's row and its retry's row must both exist and be separately attributable to burned versus delivered work
